title: How authors organise ideas
log: 2026-11-04T09:36:49Z write: the API refused it in the chapter request, so it is written on its own next

draft.title: How authors organise ideas
card: Authors choose the order of their ideas on purpose. The order can shape what a reader thinks and feels.
the text first shows an issue, then offers a way to fix it. This makes the reader feel the issue matters and the fix is sensible.
the text sets two things side by side, showing how they are alike or different. This helps the reader judge which is better.
the text builds up to its strongest point, which comes last. This leaves the reader with the biggest idea fresh in mind.
draft.remember: The order of ideas is a choice, and it guides how a reader responds.

a.q: A writer opens with litter choking a local creek, then ends by suggesting a bin and a clean-up day. How are the ideas organised?
opts: As a list of unrelated facts
a.why: The text starts with an issue, the littered creek, and then offers a fix. That is a problem and solution order. It is not a comparison, because it does not set two things side by side.
a.clue: Look at what comes first and what comes last.

b.q: An article about a school's new phone rule gives a small point about tidy lockers, then a point about fewer lost phones, and ends on better learning in class. Why might the writer end this way?
opts: To finish on the strongest point so it stays with readers
To show two things side by side so readers can compare
To describe an issue before offering a fix for it
To put the weakest idea last so readers forget it
b.why: The points build from least to most important, so the strongest idea comes last and stays in the reader's mind. It is not a comparison, because the points are not two things set side by side.
b.clue: Think about which point the reader reads last, and how big it is.

b.best: To finish on the strongest point so it stays with readers
